## Description

**What**: Phase 0 administrative gate that closes 1083-fb3d as superseded (re-parenting or closing each child) and resolves e407-d35c as either closed-as-duplicate of 170b-2ac9 or scoped-as-distinct.
**Why**: Avoids orphaned descendants and duplicate ticket relationships discovered during scrutiny pipeline. Clears the dependency-section's Phase 0 gate.

**Scope**:
- IN: Run `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list-descendants 1083-fb3d`; for each child, close-as-superseded or re-parent under f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d
- IN: Resolve e407-d35c relationship via direct comparison with 170b-2ac9; close-as-duplicate or write a brief scope-distinction comment on both
- OUT: Implementing 1083-fb3d's PR-creation work (subsumed into S6 — Verified: scope explicitly assigned to S6 in epic Approach Phase 3)
- OUT: Brainstorming e407-d35c if it turns out to be distinct (file follow-on epic; do not block this epic)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, 1083-fb3d is in status `closed` with reason `Superseded by f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d`
  ← Satisfies: "Disambiguation required before sprint: 1083-fb3d (PR-based merge) — this epic absorbs PR-creation scope"
- When this story is complete, e407-d35c is either in status `closed` with reason `Duplicate of 170b-2ac9` or has a comment documenting scope-distinction from 170b-2ac9
  ← Satisfies: "Disambiguation gate (Phase 0): e407-d35c (possible duplicate of 170b-2ac9) — must be closed-as-duplicate or scoped-as-distinct before sprint kickoff"

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint operator, the disambiguation gate clears 1083-fb3d and e407-d35c so this epic can enter sprint without orphaned ticket relationships
